title: The Snowboard Shop Whose Software Became Shopify
conflicts: Build time of the Snowdevil store: two months (Lütke to Signal v. Noise, 2010) against close to four months (his own Rails community post at the January 2005 launch, quoted by Larry MacDonald); the story gives both. First-sale date misprinted as November 2014 in MacDonald's excerpt; the story says late 2004. Garage (Globe 2012) against coffee shop (Globe 2014, MacDonald); the story uses the coffee shop. Friends-and-family money: 'a bit' (Lütke, 2010) against about $200,000 (Globe 2014, Entrepreneur); the story uses the figure. Lake's exit: 2008 (Globe 2014) against 'shortly after launch' (Entrepreneur); the story uses 2008.
notes: Funding changed from the slate's 'bootstrapped' to 'mixed': friends-and-family equity plus a $250,000 angel investment (Signal v. Noise itself withdrew the interview from its no-funding series for this reason). Daniel Weinand, often listed as a third co-founder, is not in the founder field; the episode turns on Lütke and Lake. The $8,000 October 2006 revenue is Lake's recollection, as the Globe says.
